Due to the paucity of collections, the phenology of this species is poorly known; it is suspected that flowering and fruiting is influenced by the timing and intensity of rainfall events. In nature a single flowering specimen has been collected in late July, at which time the plants also possessed near-mature pods, and a separate fruiting specimen with mature seed has been collected in mid-October. In cultivation at Kings Park and Botanic Garden, Perth, plants have been observed at peak anthesis in early April and possessed mature seeds around September.
